entries.note: OntoUML has no way to add a member to a generalization set while omitting only the OWL disjointness, so the pitfall is modelled as a second, non-disjoint generalization set {Tiger} with the same categorizer. Under the profile rule (disjoint+complete -> gufo:partitions, otherwise gufo:categorizes) that set yields gufo:categorizes. Upstream states only gufo:partitions. The extra triple is entailment-neutral for the pitfall (gufo:partitions already implies the categorization), and it is not what the rule OG-UFO-PARTITION-DISJOINT or gufoshapes detect. Pending NEMO review of the OntoUML encoding of this pitfall.

entries.note: OntoUML has no instance level and cannot type an individual by a gUFO class directly, so the reified participation of the prose (':JordanLeeParticipationInFinal a gufo:Participation ; gufo:isEventProperPartOf :Final2026') is modelled as an «event» class MatchParticipation that is the part end of a «participational» relation to Match; GEX-MAP-014 makes it rdfs:subClassOf gufo:Participation. The individual is typed :MatchParticipation, from which Pellet derives the upstream ':JordanLeeParticipationInFinal a gufo:Participation' (ENTAILED-BY-ONTOGRAPH). The class itself is extra.

entries.note: Upstream links JordanLee to the reified participation with :participatedInMatch, whose rdfs:range is :Match; under OWL semantics that classifies :JordanLeeParticipationInFinal as a :Match as well as a gufo:Participation, i.e. the participation would be a match. OntoGraph checks link endpoints against the relation's end classes (OG-GUFO-INSTANCE-LINK-TYPE), so the OntoUML model uses a separate unnamed «participation» relation Player -> MatchParticipation, projected as gufo:participatedIn. Reported to NEMO as a possible modelling slip in the upstream example; pending review.
